div.head: Episode 47: The TEI Processing Model — Tremendous Markup for Tremendous People

sp.speaker: Chad Markupsen
sp.p: Welcome back to Very Tremendous Texts, the podcast where big men talk about big data. I'm your host Chad Markupsen, coming to you in medias res from our luxury studio in Mar-a-Lago. Today's guests need no introduction, but I'll give them one anyway because we need the runtime. Please welcome President Donald Trump and, joining us via secure — allegedly — satellite from Moscow, President Vladimir Putin!

sp.speaker: Donald Trump
sp.p: Thank you, Chad. Fantastic show. The best show. I watch it all the time. Many people are saying this is the most important podcast about markup languages ever produced. And I know about markup — believe me, nobody marks up better than me. I once marked up a beautiful piece of vellum in a medieval scriptorium at Trump Tower. Tremendous.

sp.speaker: Vladimir Putin
sp.p: Privet, Chad. I am very happy to be here. In Russia, we have long tradition of encoding texts. Entire archives were once encoded in special way using only physical redaction — what you in West call black marker. The TEI Processing Model is, I must say, significant improvement.

div.head: Part I: What Even Is the TEI Processing Model?

sp.speaker: Chad Markupsen
sp.p: So let's dive in. Mr. President — the first one, the better one — can you explain to our listeners what the TEI Processing Model actually is?

sp.speaker: Donald Trump
sp.p: Great question, Chad, really great. So — and I understand this better than most people, I went to WhartonHe mentions this approximately once per minute. — the TEI Processing Model is essentially, you have your XMLExtensible Markup Language, right, which is already very beautiful, very strong markup, and then you say: how do we render this? And the ODD — which stands for One Document Does-it-all, very smart people came up with that name — it lets you define behaviours. Like, you say: this persName element? Make it red. Boom. Done. Nobody does behaviours better than me, Chad. My behaviours are incredible.

sp.speaker: Vladimir Putin
sp.p: This is mostly correct accurate enough. In Russia, we also appreciate the concept of model in processing. When I was in KGBHe mentions this approximately never, officially., we had very sophisticated processing model. Input: donositel' informant. Process: . Output: positive outcome. Very efficient pipeline. The TEI model is similar but with more Gemütlichkeit.

sp.speaker: Chad Markupsen
sp.p: Right. Moving on. President Putin, your team has reportedly been using TEI Publisher to encode historical documents. Can you tell us about that?

sp.speaker: Vladimir Putin
sp.p: Yes. We have been encoding the complete works of Leo Tolstoy — War and Peace, Anna Karenina, all of them. Very long texts. The processing model allows us to render different editions differently with same ODD file. This is very elegant. I am told even Tolstoy himself would have approved, though of course he is dead, so he has no choise no choice.

sp.speaker: Donald Trump
sp.p: I've read War and Peace. Whole thing. Twice. [Editor's note: no evidence supports this claim] Fantastic book, very long, some people say too long, I like it though. Very much like my speeches, which are also very long and also have a dénouement. Mine's better though. My dénouement is the best.

div.head: Part II: The Technical Details (Mostly Correct)

sp.speaker: Chad Markupsen
sp.p: Let's get technical. The TEI Processing Model uses behaviours defined in an ODD file to specify how elements should be rendered. For example, a note element might have a behaviour of footnote or margin. Can either of you give an example of a behaviour you'd like to see applied to political discourse?

sp.speaker: Donald Trump
sp.p: Great question. Great question. If I were designing the ODDOne Document Does-it-all for, let's say, the New York Times — which is failing thriving, Fake News — I would give the persName behaviour of inline for most people but for me, for Donald J. Trump, I would use a custom behaviour: renderAsGold. And it would be gold. Real gold. The best gold rendering in the history of digital humanities.

sp.speaker: Vladimir Putin
sp.p: This is interesting proposal. In my design, I would apply behaviour omit selectively. Certain persName elements would simply . You understand. It is a matter of gosudarstvennaya bezopasnost' state security. The processing model is very flexible in this regard. I appreciate the predicate functionality — you can apply different behaviours depending on context. Very useful. Very useful.

sp.speaker: Chad Markupsen
sp.p: That's... certainly one interpretation of conditional behaviour application. Mr. Trump, what about the output modes in TEI Publisher? You can render the same document as HTMLHyperText Markup Language, PDFPortable Document Format, even ePubElectronic Publication. Does that resonate with you?

sp.speaker: Donald Trump
sp.p: Absolutely, Chad, and I'll tell you why. I have many output modes myself. There's rally mode — very high energy. There's tête-à-tête mode, very intimate, very classy. And there's executive order mode — one document, does it all, everybody has to comply, very similar to the ODD concept now that I think about it. I invented that, actually. The concept. Not the ODD specifically, but the idea of one thing controlling everything. That was me. People are saying that.

sp.speaker: Vladimir Putin
sp.p: I would like to conclude by saying that the TEI Processing Model represents a triumph of structured thinking over chaos. In a world of unvalidated documents and missing schema references, the ODD provides certainty. Order. Control. Beautiful control. This is something I ценю value deeply.

sp.speaker: Donald Trump
sp.p: I agree with Vladimir, which I rarely do — he's a tough negotiator, very tough — but on TEI we are totally aligned. Totally. The processing model is, frankly, one of the great achievements of the last forty years. Maybe the greatest. Bigger than the moon landing. Many people are saying. And I want to tell everyone listening: get into TEI. Learn your behaviours. Read your ODD. It's going to be so good. So so So very tremendously good.

sp.speaker: Chad Markupsen
sp.p: Profound. Truly. Thank you both. This has been Episode 47 of Very Tremendous Texts. If you enjoyed today's episode, please subscribe, leave a five-star review, and consider donating to the Digital Humanities Emergency Fund for Endangered Angle Brackets A real organisation. Probably. We didn't check.. Until next time: encode responsibly, validate often, and remember — well-formed is just the beginning.

div.head: Glossary of Terms (For Listeners New to Both TEI and Geopolitics)

list.item: A mechanism defined within an ODD file that specifies how TEIText Encoding Initiative elements should be rendered in various output formats. Not, despite what was implied above, invented by Mr. Trump.
One Document Does-it-all. A TEIText Encoding Initiative customisation file combining schema and documentation. Does not grant executive powers.

An instruction in the processing model specifying how an element should be transformed. Common values include inline, block, footnote, omit, and the newly proposed renderAsGold [not yet in the TEI Guidelines].
See Putin, V., remarks passim. Not a TEI term.
